$comment: Team is a logical source: on both platforms it selects native users with showOnWebsite ticked, never a separate post type or collection. Apply that filter to every team query and manual selection, not to post credit. A ticked user needs no admin access. Editors may manage public profiles, but that permission must not let them create or manage accounts, roles, credentials or security fields. Ticking the box grants no account permissions. The public page at /team/{slug}/ reads the person fields and the member's posts, if any. Team has no topics (SC-027), no collection index page and no view-all link. The editor's order is each platform's own.
label: Team member

fields.name: showOnWebsite
fields.label: Team member
fields.description: Include this user in team selections and give them a public profile. This neither grants admin access nor changes post credit.

fields.name: slug
fields.label: Public profile slug
fields.description: The unique public slug for /team/{slug}/. A ticked user needs one. It is independent of the login and stays the same when the display name changes.

dropped.note: The member's own page reads the bio field (contract/collections/_person.json), not the post content, which stays dropped (the founder's ruling of 19/11/2026).
Unread, and team has no categories (SC-027). Salt for Next.js may keep it as a site extra.

display.$comment: Derived from Salt for Next.js's READ_CARD and Salt for WordPress's inc/sections/team.php, with the rc.7 names. Salt for Next.js's core card draws no contact links today; markup/card.json draws them when filled (SC-006).

href.note: The member's own page at /team/{slug}/, using the stable public slug.

email.note: Drawn as a mailto: link when filled.

phoneHref.note: The tel: address, only when the phone normalises to one.

profiles.note: Each row in order: name names the link, url is its address, and the network is derived from the address (contract/socials.json).
